transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. That pulsing behaviour is usually the vacuum's safety system kicking in because airflow is restricted (a blockage) or the filters are damp/clogged. Since your battery is full, we can rule out a simple power issue. Please detach the wand and floorhead from the main body. Look through each tube and check inside the bin inlet for any obstructions like hair, dust balls, or debris. Clear anything you find. Let me know if you found a blockage or if everything looked clear.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
its a v8 animal. took the wand off, big clump of hair and cat litter stuck at the bottom where the head goes on, pulled it out. no burning smell or heat tho

[Heading: Airflow restriction (blockage)]
Good work finding that blockage—that hair and litter clump would have restricted airflow enough to trigger the vacuum's safety system, causing it to cut out and pulse as it tried to reset. However, if the filters are clogged or even slightly damp from previous cleaning, they can cause the same pulsing issue by restricting airflow further down the line. Please check the pre-motor filter and the post-motor (HEPA) filter in the body of the vacuum. If they look dirty or haven't been washed recently, wash them under cold water (no soap), shake off excess water, and leave them to dry completely for at least 24 hours before putting them back. Once you've done that (or if they are already clean and fully dry), try running the vacuum again. If it runs steadily now, you're all set. If it still stutters after a full dry cycle of the filters, let me know.
washed the filter, water came out black lol. left it overnight on the radiator side. its fine now, proper suction, no pulsin

[Heading: Blocked airflow cleared]
That’s excellent news. The combination of the hair/litter blockage and the very dirty filters was restricting airflow enough to trigger the vacuum's safety cut-out, causing it to pulse on and off. Since you’ve cleared the blockage and washed the filters (and they are now dry), the airflow is restored and the motor can run steadily again. Just a quick tip for next time: always ensure the filters are completely bone-dry before putting them back in; even slight dampness can cause similar pulsing issues. If this happens again, check for blockages first, then inspect the filters. You should be good to go!
